The claim for compensation raised in the present claim petition is in respect of fatal injuries alleged to have been sustained by the deceased Sh. Om Prakash in a motor accident that took place on 06.01.2019, at about 9:30 am, Near Karan Gate, Police Chowki, PS Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, U.P.,
regarding which one FIR No. 0084/2019, under Sections 279/338 IPC was registered at PS Sahibabad, Ghaziabad.

The vehicle involved in this case is a truck bearing registration No.
NL-03AA-0579, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no.1 (R1) Sh.
Arun Kumar Yadav, owned by respondent no. 2 (R2) Smt. Indra Devi and insured with respondent no. 3 (R3) Edelweiss General Insurance Co. Ltd.
2.
It is the case of the petitioners that on 06.01.2019 at around 9:30 AM, the deceased was peddling bicycle from Garima Garden, Ghaziabad towards Sahibabad Vegetable Market (Subji Mandi).

When he reached near Karan Gate, Police Chowki, Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, U.P., all of a sudden, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. NL-03AA-0579, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, hit the bicycle of deceased due to which the deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
It is further stated that the deceased succumbed to his injuries sustained in the accident.

3. Respondent no. 1 and 2 filed their joint written statement to the DAR wherein it is stated that the alleged offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no. 3 w.e.f. 16.11.2018 to 15.11.2019.
It is further stated that the respondent no. 1 was holding a valid driving license, permit and fitness certificate at the time of accident.

It is pertinent to mention that R-1 and R-2 were proceeded against ex-parte vide Order dated 10.05.2023.
4.

Respondent no. 3/Insurance Company filed its written statement to the claim petition wherein it is stated that the alleged offending vehicle was duly insured with them in the name of respondent no. 2 w.e.f. 16.11.2018 to 15.11.2019.

It is further stated that the accident had taken place due to negligence of deceased himself as he was not following the traffic rules and regulations while plying his bicycle at the time of accident.

5. On 16.02.2022, the following issues were framed by this tribunal as:-
1. Whether the deceased sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 06.01.2019, at about 09:30 am, Near Karan Gate, Police Chowki, PS Sahibabad,
Ghaziabad, U.P. caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. NL-03AA-0579 being driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 ?

OPP.

6. In support of their claim, the petitioner no. 1 Smt. Sunita Kushvaha has examined herself as PW1.
Her affidavit in evidence is Ex. PW1/A.
She relied upon certain documents.
Copy of Aadhaar cards of petitioners are Ex. PW1/1 (colly) (OSR).
Copy of Aadhaar card of deceased as Ex. PW1/2 (OSR).

Certified copies of criminal case record are Ex. PW1/3 (colly).
7.
The petitioners have also examined one Sh. Puran as PW2.
His affidavit in evidence is Ex. PW2/A.
He relied upon certain documents.
Copy of his Aadhaar card is Ex. PW2/1(OSR).
Certified copy of FIR already Ex. PW1/3 (colly).
8. However, no witness was examined by the respondents in rebuttal.

9. The Tribunal heard the arguments advanced by Sh. Shekhar Aggarwal, Ld. Counsel for petitioners and Ms. Vandana Kahlon, Ld. Counsel for R-3/Insurance Company and has carefully perused the entire case record along with written submissions filed on behalf of petitioners and Insurance Company.
The findings on the aforementioned issues are rendered hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs.

1. Whether the deceased sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 06.01.2019, at about 09:30 am, Near Karan Gate, Police Chowki, PS Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, U.P. caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. NL-03AA-0579 being driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 ? OPP.
11. Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.

The first question that needs to be decided is whether the accident was caused by the vehicle bearing registration No. NL- 03AA-0579.
12.

In his affidavit in evidence Ex. PW2/A, PW2 has narrated the incident as follows :-
"1. That on 06.01.2019 at about 09:30 A.M. Sh. Om Prakash S/o Late Sh. Chhaddu was going on his cycle and was proceed towards Sahibabad Sabzi Mandi from his house Garima Garden, when reached near Karan Gate police chowki, Sahibabad,
Ghaziabad then a truck bearing No. NL03AA0579 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner without caring of the rules of the traffic came from back side and hit the cyclist as a result of forceful impact the cyclist fell down on the road and sustain serious/grievous injuries.
2. That after the accident the public persons gathered on spot and the driver of the truck ran away from the spot after leave the truck.

The injured was removed to Narender Mohan Hospital & Heart Centre, Mohan Nagar, Ghaziabad from the spot of accident but the condition of the injured was very serious so he was referred to Sunita Kushvaha And Ors vs Arun Kumar Yadav And Ors on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7660927/
3

Safdarjung Hospital, Delhi but during the course of treatment the injured Sh. Om Prakash succumbed due to the injuries sustained in the accident on the same day i.e.
06.01.2019.

3. That a FIR No. 0084/2019 U/s 279/338, P.S. Sahibabad, Distt. Ghaziabad, U.P.
was registered on my complaint on the same day i.e. 06.01.2019 against the driver of the truck.
4. That this accident was caused due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of the truck bearing No. NL03AA0579."
13. PW2 also deposed that after the accident, the driver of the truck ran away.

In his cross examination, he has deposed as follows :-
"There is a divider on the road dividing the incoming and outgoing traffic.
At one point of time 3 vehicles can ply on one side of the road.
My auto was on the leftmost side of the road.
I cannot tell the number of the auto.
At the time of accident, I was going to fetch the vegetables.
My brother in law was on the cycle in the leftmost lane of the road.
I was far behind and there was a lot of crowd gathered at the spot of the accident.
It is correct that the accident had already taken place and which is why a lot of crowd was gathered there.
The accident had already taken place and I did not see the truck driver as he ran away and I saw the driver running away.
I could not see him properly.
The truck driver left the truck behind."
14. The testimony of PW2 is natural.
He himself did not see the accident taking place but he did see the driver of the truck running away.
15. I shall now refer to the site plan.
In the site plan, two spots have been shown at point X and point B near the roundabout.
It is mentioned in the site plan that point X is the place where the injured got fatal injuries after forceful impact by the offending vehicle.
B is shown as place of accident.
They have been shown close to each other.
From the site plan, it is not clear whether the truck came into the lane of cyclist or cyclist came into the lane of the truck or if the truck hit the cycle sideways.
In absence of any eye witness, only R-1/driver of the offending vehicle could have explained the circumstances which led to the accident in question.
R-1 never entered the witness box.
16. As per the chargesheet, the investigation disclosed that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent act of R-1/driver of the offending vehicle.

17. In cases National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court

sentences.text: It has been further observed that even when the accused were to be acquitted in the criminal case, the same may be of no effect on the assessment of the liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal.

20. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the petitioners and the petitioners were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
21.

owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents.

sentences.text: The compensation to which the petitioners are entitled shall be under the heads as discussed hereinafter.
(i) Loss of dependency 25.

The petitioner No. 1 being wife of the deceased stepped into the witness box as PW1 and filed her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW1/A wherein, she claimed that her deceased husband was working as labour and earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
However, no document to this effect has been placed on record.

During cross examination, she admitted that her husband and the claimants are permanent residents of Ghaziabad, U.P.
26.

Since the employment and income of the deceased has not been established on record, the minimum wages of unskilled person is taken into account as per rates prevalent in U.P., which was Rs. 7,675/- per month at the time of accident as the deceased and claimants are residents of U.P.
27.
In order to prove the age of deceased, PW1 has tendered on record copy of Aadhaar card of deceased as Ex. PW1/2 (OSR) in which the year of birth of deceased is mentioned as 1971.

Hence,
going by this document, the age of deceased as on the date of accident i.e. on 06.01.2019 was around 48 years.

In terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors.
Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been approved by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680, the multiplier of '13' is applicable in the present case.
28.

sentences.text: Now coming to calculation of loss of dependency, the present claim petition has been filed by five petitioners i.e. wife and children of deceased.

Hence, in terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors. (Supra) and Pranay Sethi & Ors. (Supra), 1/4th of earnings of deceased shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
29. Further, in view of the law laid down in the case of Pranay Sethi & Ors. (Supra), the petitioners are also held entitled to addition of 25% of earning of the deceased towards future prospects.

Thus,
the loss of dependency in the petitioners case comes to Rs.11,22,469/- (rounded off) {(Rs.7,675/-X 12 X 13 X 3/4 X 125/100)}.
(ii) COMPENSATION UNDER NON-PECUNIARY HEADS 30.

From the site plan, it is not clear whether the truck came into the lane of cyclist or cyclist came into the lane of the truck or if the truck hit the cycle sideways.
In absence of any eye witness, only R-1/driver of the offending vehicle could have explained the circumstances which led to the accident in question.
17. In cases National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court
Reliance is being placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Meera Devi & ors., 2021 LawSuit (Del) 2021 wherein it was held that "......in view of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008, contents of DAR has to be presumed to be correct and read in evidence without formal proof of the same unless proof to the contrary was produced."
19. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.
20. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.
Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the petitioners and the petitioners were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
21.
Pertinently, respondent no. 1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to rebut his involvement in the aforesaid accident, which he has failed to do.
Therefore,
an adverse inference is drawn against the respondent no.1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi)
310.
22.
In view of foregoing discussion, it stands proved on preponderance of probability that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration no. NL-03AA-0579 and the said vehicle at that time was driven by respondent no. 1,
owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents.
